findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Fresh-thread retry reads the result box before it checks liveness: a read-back that completes in that window refuses an honest account for good, and the refusal says '3 read-backs failed alike'
findings.evidence: src/engcore/mind/world/owners.py:520-525 at 3b407ddb: `thread.join(self.WAIT_S)` / `result = box.get("result")` / `if result is None: if thread.is_alive(): raise OwnerUnavailable(...)` / `return None, [_Failed("the read-back on a fresh thread did not complete", None, False, False)]`. If the fresh thread finishes after line 521 but before line 523, `is_alive()` is False and the code returns one synthetic non-recursion failure. In _account (owners.py:473-484) that failure fails the `all(f.recursion ...)` test (477), is not moving, and gives `len({(why,text)}) == 1`, so it reaches line 483: `_Unreadable(f"{what} ... ({_ATTEMPTS} read-backs failed alike): the read-back on a fresh thread did not complete")`. _read_back maps that to `_NotRead(..., True)` (owners.py:540-541), and _observe_all writes it into `self._diverged` (583-587): refused by this reader from then on. The same path is taken when the fresh thread dies from a BaseException raised in account code. Claims this contradicts: README section 4 lines 189-191 ('so a verification's own deep call stack never refuses an honest account for good ... classified by the same rule') and line 216 ('Concurrent verifications never refuse for good an account that only moved forward and that its owner reads back'); owners.py docstring 370-372.
findings.reproduction: Static reading. Not executed (lens E is static). A deterministic probe outline: a following reader over the battery fixture. The experiment's to_dict raises RecursionError on the calling thread and on the 'budget-read-back' thread sleeps WAIT_S+0.05 before returning real(). Monkeypatch threading.Thread.is_alive to join the thread before it answers, which stands in for a preemption between owners.py:521 and :523. Expected: OwnerUnavailable whose text contains '(3 read-backs failed alike): the read-back on a fresh thread did not complete' and 'from then on', reader._diverged is non-empty, and a later read at normal depth is still refused.
findings.why: The trigger is a deep caller stack together with a fresh-thread read-back that finishes about WAIT_S later; README section 8 measures large-experiment read-backs at 0.45 s alone and seconds under load. In that case an honest account that only moved forward, and that its owner can read back (the fresh thread may even have succeeded), is refused by that reader for good. The refusal reason is also wrong: it reports three alike failures that never happened. This fails closed (no wrong admission), so it is MINOR. It is still a correctness defect of the budget follower in the newest change (R12-4/R12-5), and it breaks two stated guarantees.
findings.fix: Check liveness first and read the box afterwards: `alive = thread.is_alive(); result = box.get("result")`. If alive, raise OwnerUnavailable. Once the thread has stopped the box is final, so read the result. For 'stopped with no result' (a BaseException on the fresh thread), give an honest reason ('the fresh-thread read-back raised an interruption') and treat it as not read back (length floor) rather than as three alike failures. Add a deterministic control that patches is_alive as described above.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: The guarantee that an abandoned fresh thread 'reaches nothing the reader holds' (private cache) has no effective regression control, and a regression reopens the R11-C-F1/R12-1 outcome class
findings.evidence: owners.py:505 `cache = dict(self._readback)` (a private copy) and 526-527 (adopted only when the thread finished with a result). owners.py:576 iterates `snapshot._readback.items()` inside the locked comparison before any observation is recorded. README section 5 lines 352-354: '`shared_cache` (the fresh thread writing the snapshot's cache instead of a private copy) passes every test ... (recorded, not claimed as controlled)'. docs/work/evidence/br11_local_2026_10_23/mutation/summary.txt: '[shared_cache] 666 passed, 1 skipped'. README line 191-192 states the guarantee: 'what it does later reaches nothing the reader holds (round 12)'.
findings.reproduction: Static reading, plus the committed mutation summary (read, not re-run). Under the shared_cache mutant, an abandoned thread inserting a new key into snapshot._readback while owners.py:576 iterates it raises RuntimeError inside `with self._changed:`. That happens after this verification's ticket was discarded (573) and before any history is recorded, so the error leaves pinned() (721). _Memo._pin_now keeps it, and admission raises a RuntimeError that Authorities.check does not catch (authority.py:292-297). A deterministic control is feasible without scheduling the race: block the fresh thread past WAIT_S, keep the snapshot that reader.pinned() returns, release and join the thread, then assert the snapshot's _readback did not gain its entry (or that the thread's cache is not the snapshot's dict).
findings.why: The private copy is what keeps the comparison from raising mid-way. If it regressed, a verification that read back a spend would leave without recording it. Waiters would also not be told, because the ticket was already discarded at 573 (see E13-F7). A later restore would then be re-admitted: the unobserved-spend, duplicate-dispatch class rated MAJOR in rounds 11 and 12. Under the verdict rules, an authority guarantee for Q4 with no effective regression control keeps Q4 PARTIAL. It is MINOR because the shipped code holds (static reading of 505/526).
findings.fix: Add the deterministic property control described above. Optionally, copy the cache at the comparison with `dict(snapshot._readback)` taken before the loop as defence in depth, and keep the claim in README section 5 as 'controlled' only once a mutant fails a test.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: A verification is removed from the in-flight set before its comparison loop, so one interrupted inside the comparison is treated by its waiters as compared
findings.evidence: owners.py:572-575: `with self._changed: self._in_flight.discard(ticket); self._changed.notify_all(); pending = ...` runs BEFORE the per-key loop (577-614) that records `_seen`/`_reached`/`_diverged`. _leave (owners.py:643-652) marks waiters only `if handed and ticket in self._in_flight`, and the ticket is already gone. A waiter's predicate (619) `waiter[1] or not pending & self._in_flight` is then true with waiter[1] False, so it proceeds to the post-wait re-check (630-634) on whatever was recorded. README section 4 lines 201-202 and the accepted residual say that a verification handed accounts that left without comparing makes its waiters decide on no account ('which only the verifications then waiting for it refuse').
findings.reproduction: Static reading. Not executed. It needs an exception inside the locked loop: an asynchronous KeyboardInterrupt on the main thread, a MemoryError, or any regression of the kind E13-F2 describes.
findings.why: If a verification P holding a spend is interrupted after line 573 and before it records that key, a waiting verification D holding a restored earlier state is not refused and decides on its own state. That re-opens the re-dispatch path the wait was built to close, which the documented residual says the waiters refuse. The trigger is narrow and undemonstrated (MINOR), but it is a correctness gap in Q4's forward-only mechanism and differs from the documented residual's stated behaviour.
findings.fix: Discard the ticket after the comparison loop, still under the same lock, or wrap the loop in try/except BaseException that marks this ticket's waiters (waiter[1] = True) before re-raising.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: A handed state that is not read back contributes only its length: a later rewrite at least that long is accepted, which a successful read-back would have refused for good (less information gives a more permissive outcome)
findings.evidence: owners.py:549-556 (_length counts entries only), 588-590 (only `self._reached[key] = max(...)` is recorded), 597-607 (rewrite detection compares only against `_seen`, the read-back histories). README section 4 lines 228-230 (new in 33258438, not pre-accepted): 'only their number is observed, so a later state at least that long that differs in them is not detected as a rewrite; a re-dispatch of what such a state recorded is refused, since returning to the state it was admitted on is going behind that length'.
findings.reproduction: Static reading. Scenario: seen=[a,b]. A handed spend state [a,b,c] is not read back (torn or timed out), so reached=3. The execution side restores [a,b] and settles d, giving [a,b,d] with length 3 >= reached, which extends seen: accepted, and a fresh admission is decided on a ledger that dropped c. If [a,b,c] had been read back, [a,b,d] would be refused for good (owners.py:597-601). Re-dispatch of the original AdmittedAction is still refused (its bound digest requires the length-2 state, which is behind), as the README says.
findings.why: This is the asymmetry the 'UNKNOWN never improves an answer' rule guards against: not being able to read a handed state makes a later rewrite acceptable that full information would refuse for good. It is strictly narrower than the owner-accepted residual (the content of a state not handed-and-read-back is never observed), and 33258438 only adds protection, so I do not count it as a new wrong outcome or as what holds Q4 PARTIAL. The sentence 'a re-dispatch of what such a state recorded is refused' is broader than what is shown: it holds for the admitted action's own re-dispatch, not for a new admission on a rewritten timeline.
findings.fix: Without running account code, also record each unread entry's owner identity: a BudgetCharge's charge_id or a ScientificEvaluation's evaluation_id, read through `object.__getattribute__(entry, '__dict__')` and required to be exact str. Treat a later state whose first N identities differ as a rewrite (refused for good). Honest torn moves keep their ids. Otherwise narrow the README sentence to 're-dispatch of the action admitted on an earlier state'.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Report and docstring overstate the round-12 classification: a BaseException raised by account content leaves the classification with no trace (no length floor), and `str(exc)` does run the failure's own code
findings.evidence: README section 4 lines 186-187: 'A failure is described without running any code of it that could raise ... so no read-back failure leaves the classification (round 12)'. owners.py:368-369 says the same. README section 9 line 505 (R12-3): 'Fixed generically: any state not read back observes its account's length'. README section 4 line 174-175: 'Execution-side code runs only inside the owner's own serialization and read-back'. Code: _read_once catches only `Exception` (owners.py:458). _described runs `str(exc)`, the failure's own __str__ (owners.py:129), and catches only Exception. BudgetCharge passes `detail`/`predicted` through unchanged (sria/campaign/budget.py:113,125,130), so the json.dumps default=str at owners.py:432-433 runs str() on execution-side objects. A BaseException subclass raised there passes through _attempts/_account/_read_back (539-546 catch only _Unreadable/OwnerUnavailable), leaves pinned() before _length runs, and is not caught by _Memo._pin_now (authority.py:383-387, catches Exception), so every admission raises.
findings.reproduction: Static reading. Not executed. Example: an executor settles a charge whose `detail` object's __str__ raises a BaseException subclass. findings.why: The owner accepted this as 'interrupted (a BaseException ...)', so it is not filed as a new MAJOR. findings.fix: Qualify the three statements ('any Exception'; '__str__ is run and its Exception caught'). State in the residual that a BaseException from account content is included. findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Abandoned fresh threads are never reclaimed: an account that recurses on the calling thread and blocks on the fresh one leaks one daemon thread (and one cache copy) per verification
findings.evidence: owners.py:504-524: every verification whose three calling-thread attempts all hit recursion starts a new daemon thread and abandons it after WAIT_S. Nothing bounds how many can be alive at once. README section 4 lines 190-192 says only that what the thread does later 'reaches nothing the reader holds'.
findings.reproduction: Static reading. An execution side that verifies from a deep stack while holding a lock its account's serialization takes, for a long stretch (b1207/a1207's pattern), or account code that blocks forever on threads named 'budget-read-back', starts one new blocked thread holding `dict(self._readback)` per verification.

findings.fix: Keep at most one outstanding fresh read-back per account key (reuse it, or refuse while one is alive), and document the residual in README sections 4 and 8.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: A spend in a handed state that is never read back is observed only as a length: after a restore plus one more charge, the executed action is admitted and dispatched again, where a readable spend is refused for good
findings.evidence: owners.py@3b407ddb:542-546 (_read_back records only _NotRead(why, False, length) for OwnerUnavailable), 549-556 (_length: len of charges/_evaluations only), 588-590 (_observe_all: self._reached = max(...length)), 597-607 (the rewrite check compares history against self._seen only; _reached gates length only). README §4:228-230 and the owners.py docstring 386-388 state that only the number is observed. The README parenthetical 'a re-dispatch of what such a state recorded is refused, since returning to the state it was admitted on is going behind that length' holds only for the original AdmittedAction. A fresh projection re-admits and dispatches the same action. Probe ~/br11-review/r13/F-round12-rewrites-deep/probes/f1302_unread_state_rewrite.py (output f1302_out.txt; source also in the Windows scratch file r13/F-round12-rewrites-deep/f1302.sh). Results: [SelfFillingNote] and [VaryingNote]: two verifications handed the spend were refused once; the original re-dispatch after the restore was refused; after charge c, the fresh projection+admission of X was FEASIBLE and DISPATCHED; X executed 2 times; _reached={solver: 2}. [control: readable spend]: the fresh projection was refused ('rewrote its history'); X executed 1 time.
findings.reproduction: cd ~/forge-r13-review && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=$HOME/forge-r13-review/src:$HOME/forge-r13-review ~/forge-gen2-authority-v1/.venv/bin/python -u ~/br11-review/r13/F-round12-rewrites-deep/probes/f1302_unread_state_rewrite.py. Steps: battery owners; BudgetReader.following; ExecutionDesk(...).gateway(). Dispatch X; the executor settles charge b whose detail always fails 'moving' (the interpreter's mutation text) or with a varying message (a note store that is unreachable, with a request counter). Two verifications are handed [a,b] and refused once with floor 2. The execution side restores the pre-run ledger by object replacement (as sria.campaign does), then settles another action's charge c, giving [a,c] with length 2. project_world(declaration, authorities) -> admit X -> gateway.dispatch: X executes a second time.
findings.why: The lens criterion is never to re-authorize what a verification was handed and the account moved past. A verification WAS handed X's spend b, and the account moved past the state X was authorized on. Because only the length of that unread state is kept, a rewritten timeline at or beyond that length ([a,c]) is accepted, and X's spend vanishes from the budget the Mind is admitted against. The forward-only rule exists to refuse exactly this rewrite: the same sequence with a readable spend is refused for good. That is an unobserved spend permitting duplicate dispatch, reproduced through the gateway. The trigger is deterministic content an execution side can hold: the round-12 b1204/b1208 values, e.g. a note whose rendering fails with a fresh request id each time. Not a regression: d40aff44 re-dispatched even on a plain restore (r12_probes_d40aff44/b1204 'DISPATCHED AGAIN'), and 33258438 only narrowed the class. The README discloses the precondition, but its 're-dispatch ... is refused' wording overstates the protection, and this statement was explicitly not owner-accepted.
findings.fix: Have the floor of an unread state also carry an identity of its first L entries that can be read without running account code: each charge's charge_id (BudgetCharge __dict__, exact str) and each evaluation's evaluation_id (both unique within an account). Treat a later read-back whose first L ids differ as a rewrite, refused for good. Alternatively, refuse for good an account whose floor was set by an unread state if a later observed state has length >= floor but does not keep those ids. Add f1302 (both note variants plus the readable control) as a gateway control asserting that X executed once. Restate README §4:228-230 so it says what is and is not refused (a fresh admission after a restore plus a charge).

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Race in the fresh-thread retry: an honest account whose read-back finishes between the join timeout and the is_alive() check is refused for good
findings.evidence: src/engcore/mind/world/owners.py:520-525 at 3b407ddb. The code does `thread.join(self.WAIT_S)`, then `result = box.get("result")`, then checks `thread.is_alive()` only when result is None. If the thread stores its result and exits after box.get but before is_alive(), the code returns `[_Failed("the read-back on a fresh thread did not complete", None, False, False)]`. In _account (owners.py:477-484) that one non-recursion, non-moving failure ends in `_Unreadable`, and _observe_all (owners.py:582-587) then puts the account in _diverged for good. The refusal text it records is false: "(3 read-backs failed alike): the read-back on a fresh thread did not complete", although the owner read the account back successfully. The README contradicts this outcome at section 4 lines 189-191 ("a verification's own deep call stack never refuses an honest account for good") and line 216 ("never refuse for good an account that only moved forward and that its owner reads back").
findings.reproduction: Probe ~/br11-review/r13/D-replay-stale/p1_race.py (script s03_race.sh). Setup: battery fixture; the main-thread to_dict raises RecursionError beyond depth+40, the same deep-stack simulation the r12 controls use; on the fresh thread the read-back is honest and takes 1.1 s. 'control' mode (nothing patched): first verification transient_timeout, a later normal-depth verification served, diverged {}. 'schedule' mode simulates the verifier being descheduled between its two checks by delaying Thread.is_alive by 0.3 s for the budget-read-back thread only: first verification FOR_GOOD, later normal-depth verification FOR_GOOD, diverged holds the experiment. Unpatched stochastic sweeps (sys.setswitchinterval(1e-6), honest completion near WAIT_S; p1_race.py sweep with 120 trials and p1c_race.py sweep_focus with 450 trials, offsets 100-260 us) produced 0 for-good outcomes: served 100+404, transient 20+46. So this is a code-level race shown only under a simulated schedule; it was not hit stochastically on CPython 3.12 with the GIL. It is more plausible in a busy multi-threaded desk (the GIL drop request is already pending when the verifier wakes) and on free-threaded builds.
findings.why: The R12-4 fix bounded the join but put the liveness check after the result check. That reopened the R12-5 class (an honest account refused for good, which needs a new reader) through a scheduling window. Fail-closed: no wrong admission or dispatch. It is still a genuine correctness defect in the budget follower, and its recorded refusal states a false cause. No control or mutant exercises a join that times out and then completes.
findings.fix: Check liveness first, then read the result: `alive = thread.is_alive(); result = box.get("result")`. If result is None and the thread is alive, raise OwnerUnavailable (not read back). If result is None and the thread is not alive, re-read box once before classifying. Treat a thread that died without a result (a BaseException) as not read back for this verification, not as three alike failures. Add a deterministic control that delays is_alive, as this probe does.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Refusal texts state false causes, and README section 4's 'a refusal says the same thing at every read, so it is recordable' does not hold for not-read-back refusals
findings.evidence: owners.py:480-482 writes "moved while it was serialized (3 read-backs failed differently)" whenever any failure carries the interpreter's mutation text. That includes an unmoving account whose three failures are byte-identical. owners.py:478-479/483-484 write "3 read-backs failed alike" after the single synthetic fresh-thread failure (see D13-1). README section 4 line 217: "A refusal says the same thing at every read, so it is recordable and replays." The not-read-back refusal embeds failures[-1].why, a message the execution side chooses, so two verifications of an unchanged state can refuse with different text.
findings.reproduction: Probe p2_floor_replay.py (script s05_floor_replay.sh), PYTHONHASHSEED 0/1/777. With DETAIL=mutation, the refusal on the spent state reads 'moved while it was serialized (3 read-backs failed differently): RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration' for a single-threaded, unmoving ledger. The record is made and replays REPRODUCED. With DETAIL=varying, steps S2 and S2b on the same unchanged state give different result digests (ce3d6701... vs 15505e3b...), and AdmissionRecord.of raises 'WorldRefused: the owners no longer give this admission'. All refusals that last are recordable and replay byte-identical across the three seeds: behind e.g. S3 93c90833.../record 89f00556...; for-good and STALE records are identical too.
findings.why: Recorded and replayed refusals carry a cause that did not happen ('moved', 'failed differently/alike'), and the README's blanket recordability claim is broader than what holds.
